glossary.Ischaemia: Too little blood flow to a tissue to meet its oxygen needs.
glossary.Thrombus: A blood clot formed inside a vessel.
glossary.Atherosclerotic plaque: A fatty, fibrous build-up in an artery wall that narrows it.
glossary.ST elevation: The ST segment raised above baseline on the ECG, a sign of full-thickness injury.
glossary.ST depression: The ST segment pushed below baseline on the ECG, a sign of ischaemia.
glossary.T wave inversion: A T wave that points downwards on the ECG, seen in ischaemia.
glossary.GTN: Glyceryl trinitrate: a spray or tablet under the tongue that widens vessels to ease angina.
glossary.Radiation: Pain spreading from where it starts to another area, such as arm or jaw.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Leads II, III, aVF: The ECG leads that look at the inferior (bottom) wall of the heart.
glossary.AV node: The relay point that passes the electrical signal from the atria to the ventricles.
glossary.Bibasal crackles: Crackles at both lung bases on listening, usually from fluid in the lungs.
glossary.Mid-systolic murmur: A heart murmur heard in the middle of systole, the contraction phase.
glossary.Pan-systolic murmur: A heart murmur heard through the whole of systole.
glossary.Tamponade physiology: Fluid around the heart squeezes it so it cannot fill, dropping cardiac output.
glossary.Muffled heart sounds: Quiet, distant heart sounds because fluid around the heart dampens them.
glossary.Right-sided failure: Failure of the right ventricle, causing raised JVP, liver swelling and leg oedema.
glossary.3rd heart sound: An extra low sound early in diastole, heard with a stiff or overloaded ventricle.
glossary.4th heart sound: An extra sound just before S1, from the atrium pushing into a stiff ventricle.
glossary.Pleuritic chest pain: Sharp chest pain that worsens on breathing in.
glossary.Sudden cardiac death: Unexpected death from heart causes, usually an arrhythmia, within an hour of symptoms.
glossary.Embolic stroke: A stroke caused by a clot or debris travelling to a brain artery.
glossary.Coronary angiography: X-ray of the coronary arteries using dye injected through a catheter.
glossary.Serial troponin: Troponin measured at two or more time points to see if it is rising.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood test of kidney function, sodium and potassium.
glossary.Chest X-ray: Plain X-ray of the chest showing lungs, heart size and fluid.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets clumping into clots, such as aspirin.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Drugs that slow blood clotting, such as heparin or fondaparinux.
glossary.Heparin: An injected anticoagulant that stops clots growing.
glossary.Sats: Oxygen saturation: the percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured by a finger probe.
glossary.Risk-stratify: Sort patients by how likely they are to have a bad outcome, to guide treatment.
glossary.Conservative management: Treating with medicines and monitoring rather than a procedure.
glossary.Reperfusion: Restoring blood flow to a blocked artery.
glossary.High-intensity statin: A strong statin dose, such as atorvastatin 80 mg, to cut LDL sharply.
glossary.Atorvastatin: A statin drug that lowers cholesterol and stabilises plaques.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that slows the heart and lowers its oxygen needs.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: Drug that blocks angiotensin II formation, lowering BP and protecting the heart after MI.
glossary.Angioplasty: Widening a narrowed artery with a balloon, usually with a stent.
glossary.Thrombogenic: Likely to trigger blood clot formation.
glossary.Platelet aggregation: Platelets sticking together to start a clot.
glossary.Necrosis: Death of cells in living tissue.
glossary.Sensitive: A test that picks up almost everyone who has the condition.
glossary.Specific: A test that is rarely positive in people without the condition.
glossary.Pericardial sac: The fibrous bag that surrounds the heart.
glossary.Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium, the sac around the heart.
glossary.Autoimmune: The immune system attacking the body's own tissue.
glossary.Antigens: Molecules the immune system recognises and reacts against.
glossary.Pulmonary oedema: Fluid in the lungs' air spaces, causing breathlessness.
glossary.Mechanical complications: Physical tears in the heart after MI: papillary muscle, septum or free wall.
